title: Cognitive Metaphors and Spatial Conceptualization in Hungarian

sections.title: Philosophical & Societal Framework
sections.content: According to George Lakoff and Mark Johnson (*Metaphors We Live By*), human thought is fundamentally metaphorical: we map concrete physical and spatial experiences onto abstract domains. Hungarian, with its 3x3 spatial case system (interior, surface, proximity), is a masterclass in cognitive spatial mapping.

sections.title: Linguistic Analysis
sections.content: Abstract states are conceived as containers: *dühbe gurul* (rolls into anger), *kétségbe esik* (falls into doubt), *bízik valakiben* (trusts inside someone). Social roles and events are surfaces: *rajta van a sor* (the turn is upon him), *konferencián vesz részt* (participates upon a conference). Path and direction structures organize decisions: *dűlőre jut* (reaches a path ridge / agreement), *kifelé áll a szénája* (his hay sticks outward / he is about to be dismissed).

sections.title: Key Conceptual Paradigms
rows: plunges into sorrow, falls into despair... (container metaphor: -ba/-be)
stands beside his principles... (postpositional loyalty schema)
reaches a cart-track, reaches a dead-end... (path & journey metaphor)
